metadata.summary: Harry Brook insists he wants to be a captain that "England fans and the team rely on" as we near the one-year anniversary of his altercation with a bouncer at a nightclub in New Zealand.
metadata.content: Harry Brook wants to be captain 'England fans can rely on', ODI skipper says ahead of Pakistan, Sri Lanka tri-series | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harry Brook wants to be captain 'England fans can rely on', ODI skipper says ahead of Pakistan, Sri Lanka tri-series Harry Brook on nightclub incident in New Zealand last year: "I know it wasn't an ideal situation to put myself in, but I feel as a captain and a leader I've learnt a lot"; England's tri-series ODI vs Pakistan, live on Sky Sports Cricket, 8.30am, Tuesday (first ball 9am) Monday 19 October 2026 12:48, UK Image: Harry Brook says he wants to be a captain that 'England fans can rely on' Harry Brook insists he wants to be a captain that "England fans and the team rely on" as we near the one-year anniversary of his altercation with a bouncer at a nightclub in New Zealand. Brook was overlooked for the Test captaincy after Ben Stokes' international retirement this summer, while he's previously admitted that he could have been sacked as white-ball skipper for the incident in Wellington that occured just hours before an ODI against the Black Caps on Halloween last year. Since then, Brook has stabilised an ailing 50-over side, with England winning their last three series - having lost seven of eight prior - while his T20 team currently top the world rankings. messages.text: Merson: Brighton defeat scared Arsenal – they won’t beat Bayern

metadata.summary: The defeat to Brighton has scared Arsenal. After winning the league, they came out and played some entertaining football, but then that result happened and they’ve gone back to being an efficient machine.
metadata.content: Arsenal were spooked by Brighton defeat and have reverted to type - they won't beat Bayern Munich, says Paul Merson | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Arsenal were spooked by Brighton defeat and have reverted to type - they won't beat Bayern Munich, says Paul Merson Sky Sports' Paul Merson pens his latest column on Arsenal's attacking issues following their narrow win over Nottingham Forest; Arsenal face Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday; Eberechi Eze's struggles continue in the Premier League Paul Merson Football Expert & Columnist @PaulMerse Monday 19 October 2026 14:14, UK The defeat to Brighton has scared Arsenal. After winning the league, they came out and played some entertaining football, but then that result happened and they’ve gone back to being an efficient machine. It frightened them and they've reverted to type. And the type is that they won't let in any goals, and they'll make an opportunity to score a goal, and that's exactly what they did at Nottingham Forest. I don't think I've ever seen a game where a team has that much possession and still doesn't look like scoring a goal in a month of Sundays. It was as bad as it gets. messages.text: Why Man Utd continue to divide opinion

metadata.summary: Michael Carrick called Sunday's draw at Leeds a 'fresh start'. Gary Neville described it as a 'stepping stone'. Most unattached observers came to another conclusion entirely.
metadata.content: Why Michael Carrick's Man Utd side continue to divide opinion following another disjointed display at Elland Road | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Why Michael Carrick's Man Utd side continue to divide opinion following another disjointed display at Elland Road Man Utd are winless in their last six games across all competitions; they stand 13th in the Premier League table, their worst start to a top-flight campaign for 40 years; Michael Carrick believes his side can still 'have a good season' - but how is success even measured these days? Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Monday 19 October 2026 15:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Premier League match between Leeds and Manchester United. Michael Carrick called Sunday's draw at Leeds a 'fresh start'. Gary Neville described it as a 'stepping stone'. Most unattached observers came to another conclusion entirely. That is Manchester United in this moment. A confusing mix of juxtapositions. A club obsessed with taking one step forward and two steps back. Only ever one result away from complete disaster. Carrick's position remains precariously poised given United have only won two of 10 games in all competitions so far this season. To speak of fresh starts as early as October surely evokes more worry than it arrests. The sentiment is understandable. But why is it necessary? messages.text: Colts fire GM Ballard after poor start to season

metadata.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have fired general manager Chris Ballard following the team's disappointing start to the 2026 NFL season.
metadata.content: Indianapolis Colts fire general manager Chris Ballard following loss to Tennessee Titans that extended poor start to NFL season | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Indianapolis Colts fire general manager Chris Ballard following loss to Tennessee Titans that extended poor start to NFL season The Indianapolis Colts suffered an upset defeat to the Tennessee Titans in Week Six to fall to 2-4 on the season as they look to end a six-year playoff drought; the Colts reached the playoffs just twice during Chris Ballard's time as General Manager Monday 19 October 2026 15:14, UK Image: Indianapolis Colts have fired general manager Chris Ballard The Indianapolis Colts have fired general manager Chris Ballard following the team's disappointing start to the 2026 NFL season. Ballard was hired as back in 2017 and departs with a record of 72-82-1 having reached the playoffs just twice during his time in charge. The Colts were beaten 26-20 by the Tennessee Titans in Week Six to fall to 2-4 as they bid to reach the playoffs for the first time since 2020. Ballard's only playoff win in Indianapolis came in the 2018-19 campaign when the Colts defeated the Houston Texans in the Wild Card round, before being eliminated by the Kansas City Chiefs the following week.
